sections.title: Category,Commodity Code, UN/SPSC and UOM Mapping
paragraphs: Sets
Mapping Sets: Configuring Category to UNSPSC, Category to Commodity Codes, UNSPSC
format, UOM Inbound and Outbound Mappings

In the 18.1 release development towards creating multiple mapping sets and then making those available for business unit designation began. The feature will be partially completed in 18.1 release. In 18.1 release, the back-end data is migrated to a new database table schema that will later on allow us to select an entire mapping set that can be related to one or more business units. (We originally thought we would be able to add the multiple mapping sets functionality per org in 18.1, however there were complications for making the multiple sets available to upstream products like TSM, Sourcing and Contract modules. Therefore, we are hiding the ability to create multiple sets in 18.1 and will continue to work on the back-end design for making more than the default set available to other modules in a later release.)

What is a mapping set? It is a set of configurations that define how products and services are classified, how product attributes are sent to an ERP system, how product attributes are interpreted when being imported into the site and how the internationally recognized UN/SPSC values should be structured in integration point messages.

In a Spend Director licensed organization, a mapping set defines how the organization wants to classify products on documents like carts, requisitions, purchase orders, invoices and receipts. In a non-spend director organization, the mapping set is only used for creating a list of commodity codes that can be used to classify suppliers, contracts or sourcing event data. Products from hosted catalogs generally have something called a identifier UN/SPSC which is used internationally to classify products and services. At JAGGAER, we classify products into a category that has a tree hierarchy. Then we map the UNSPSC numbers to these categories. An organization can choose to use the JAGGAER category to UN/SPSC mapping by default or they can choose to map the JAGGAER categories to a commodity code value. Commodity code values are generally used by the customer ERP systems for reporting purposes. If the customer wishes to map their ERP commodity code values to the JAGGAER categories for purposes of classifying spend data, then this interface is where that task is accomplished. If the customer wishes to map their ERP's standard abbreviations for units of measure to the JAGGAER abbreviations for units of measure, then this is where that task is performed. The mappings defined in a mapping set are used when sending or receiving messages with an ERP system (Enterprise Resource Planning= ERP. Examples are PeopleSoft, Oracle, SAP, Lawson, Banner Finance).

Why did we need a new database structure and a data migration? The new schema is designed so that in a future release, a Multi-Business Unit organization can specify one mapping set to use per business unit. The new schema design will also eventually allow a Non-Multi-Business Unit organization to create a new mapping set and completely configure it before making it the default for business processes.(Currently, each time an admin makes a change, that change immediately becomes live. Admins would like to fully configure all of their planned changes before switching business processes over to their new configuration.) The data from the old Manage Commodity Codes and Mappings user interface was migrated from the SciQuest database schema to a new schema called CategoryUOMMappingSets.

History is provided for logging actions taken on the mapping set. The old configurations did not have history. The new framework should be an improvement for supportability because now changes to the configuration can be tracked down.

The is modeled from the Roles management interface with a left tree navigation and the ability to hide the tree. We can hide the tree new user interface to make visual room for the main body of the mapping sets because some sections have many tabs.
Prior to 18.1:

Before release 18.1 there was no history framework for the various mappings and configurations found under Manage Commodity Codes and Mappings or under Organization Inbound and Outbound UOM Mappings. Now that we are migrating all of these pages to a new set of pages and a new database table structure, We are also making the old pages accessible to we are freezing the old pages and preventing anyone from being able to edit this data. int . This will allow the support teams and implementation teams to see what the values were pre-migration and if something did not migrate ernal users only over correctly, the internal user will be able to troubleshoot the problem.

- EP-1771 Getting issue details... STATUS In order to export or import the commodity code list values, navigate to the mapping set and then select the commodity code section from the tree view. Then select the Import/Export tab. The user should be able to export the list. Modify the CSV file and then upload the edited file for validation or import. The validation action will report back to the user as to whether there are any errors or warnings that would prevent some codes from being imported. The end user will get a file from the validatoin activity that they should download and then open. Open the file to see the specifics about any errors that were found. The validation activity also provides the ability to trigger an import of this file. The user selects the "Click to Import" link and the import process begins. Once the import is completed, the user will see a status indication of how many records were successfully imported.

paragraphs: For more information on the Units of Measure Configuration and Mappings: The configuration page of the UOM section allows the site to decide if UOM mapping is needed, how units of measure should be displayed in the site and how the units of measure on documents should be interpreted when exported or imported with an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system.

sections.title: In the old framework, these values were inherited from Default org. With the new framework this is no longer the case.
paragraphs: In the old framework, these values were inherited from Default org. With the new framework this is no longer the case. The hard coded defaults in the mapping sets will not be inherited from Default Org at all.

The hard coded default values for UOM configuration in a new org or in an org that never defined these fields: "Select to Use UOM Mapping Functionality" - off by default "Choose Display Format for Packaging UOM" default will be: UOM Only (e.g. "CS") "Outbound to ERP Integration Value" default will be: send supplier value "Default Inbound Package UOM Value" default will be: EA - Each Once decisions are made on the UOMs configuration page, then other tabs become available for creating a map between JAGGAER UOM values to the ERP system matching UOM value. Select To Use UOM Mapping Functionality: Select this checkbox to map Package UOM and Product Size UOM values for both inbound and outbound values. Choose Display Format for Packaging UOM: This setting will allow you to set how the System Packaging/UOM for an item is displayed to the user. The default setting is to simply show only the UOM code (e.g. EA, CS, etc..), however changing this setting will enable you to display the code and/or the actual description of the unit of measure. For example, if the System UOM evaluates to a "Case", then the UOM code is "CS". By default, the user would see "CS" in product search results, in favorites and in their cart. However, if you changed this setting to show "Description Only", then the user would see "Case" instead of CS. One reason you may want to make this change is when the UOMs that your shoppers are used to seeing in your ERP system don't match the System UOM values. This could cause some confusion to the shopper. For example if they saw CS, they may know that UOM as a "cassette" in their ERP, but in your site this means "case". Note: Changing this setting will only change what the user sees online. It will notchange the UOM on the order to the supplier (aka the "Supplier UOM") or the UOM value that is passed back into your ERP system (aka the "Buyer UOM").

How should the application populate UOM values in integration point export messages?Outbound to ERP Integration Value: Send system value: The send system value option will distribute the JAGGAER-mapped UOM value into the ERM. This value is the value seen in the application (Search, Non-Catalog, etc).

sections.title: Package Inbound
paragraphs: Send mapped value: The send mapped value will only appear if the Select To Use UOM Mapping Functionality checkbox is checked. This selection will send the Package UOM value that the organization has mapped.
Send supplier value: The send supplier value will send only the supplier Package UOM value in points of integration with an ERP system.

Default Inbound Package UOM Value: The value selected from this drop-down box will be used within the application when an imported UOM value does not immediately map to any of the existing mapping relationships.

Package inbound mappings might be needed if the ERP system is sending carts, requisitions, purchase orders or invoices into the site via an XML integration point. If the ERP system defines a case as CE but JAGGAER defines it as CS, then the customer organization can create a map that will cause the application to read the CE value and translate that to the CS value when parsing messages sent to the JAGGAER site. The imported documents will show the correct JAGGAER value when viewed in the user interface.

sections.title: What is a UNSPSC code?
paragraphs: For more information about UNSPSC configuration:

The United Nations Standard Products and Services Code (UNSPSC ) is a taxonomy of products and services for use in eCommerce. It is a four-level hierarchy coded as an eight-digit number, with an optional fifth level adding two more digits. The UNSPSC offers a single global classification system that can be used for: Company-wide visibility of spend analysis Cost-effective procurement optimization Full exploitation of electronic commerce capabilities Find out the details on these pages: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNSPSC
https://www.unspsc.org

Why does the UNSPSC coding system matter to JAGGAER and our customers? The UN member organizations occasionally introduce new taxonomy values. When these new taxonomy values are introduced, then JAGGAER must also update our Category list and the way we have mapped our proprietary categories to the UN code taxonomy. When suppliers in our network are loading items for a hosted catalog, they classify their items by category. They also provide the UNSPSC value as part of the item details. Punchout suppliers will send items back to our site with a UNSPSC value. The values provided on items allow the customers to then create a mapping from the JAGGAER proprietary category associated with the UNSPSC codes.

sections.title: How to configure the format in the site:
paragraphs: Suppliers use these codes to classify their products or services so that our customers buying products can more easily manage the spend per classification. Some organizations only care about tracking spend at the Segment and Family level and some may care about classifying spend at a more detailed level. Therefore, we provide them a way to decide how they want to view and export this data to their ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) systems. The UNSPSC page in the default mapping set defines how the customer site wants to view the UNSPSC code values on items and how it wants this data sent to the ERP in XML or electronic messages.

In the 18.1 release, we moved the page for configuring UNSPSC to the Default Mapping Set. Navigate to Setup > Hosted Catalog and Ordering Configuration > Category, Commodity and UOM Mapping Sets > Default Mapping Set > Select the UN/SPSC section

UN/SPSC Masking Format: This setting specifies how many segments of the code to be shown in the JAGGAER system. Some organizations only want the first two segments, in which case zeros are sent for the final two segments if sent to an external system. The UNSPSC value has 4 parts to it. The first 2 digits represent a "Segment". The next 2 digits represent a "Family". Then the two digits after that represent a "Class". The last two digits represent a "Commodity". Sometimes the customer only care about part of the UNSPSC, therefore we give them a way to only show the values for the portions they care about and populate the other portions with zeros. The site can choose to see the full UNSPSC value when they select: Use Segment-Family-Class-Commodity(nn-nn-nn-nn)

sections.title: Notes from testing - comparison between existing functions in Rambo 17.3 and Daffy 18.1:
paragraphs: UN/SPSC Separator: While testing for 18.1 we compared the way these values are exported in XML and in document search exports to the way it was done in 17.3. We found that this separator is completely ignored for exports in the 17.3 release. Therefore, we are not using these settings in 18.1 when we do an XML export of a document or when we perform a transaction or full export of a set of documents in document search. The original help text for the field in 17.3 states that the separator should be used in integration points, but since it is not working this way in 17.3 we are afraid of changing it in 18.1. Original help text: This setting identifies the separator to be displayed between segments. This is important for integration, since some systems require a specific segment separator or none at all. What we have found is that this setting is mostly used for displaying UNSPSC in the user interface in places like product details overlay. Apply to UN/SPSC Integration Value: Help text: This setting should be enabled to apply the above settings(meaning Masking format and Separator selections) to the integration messages, eg, cart return, PO, etc. The help text for this settings seems to indicate that these fields should be obeyed in exports. However, in the 17.3 release when we tested this functionality - the settings are not being obeyed on PR or PO XML exports. Apply to Commodity Code Value: Help text: This setting should be enabled to apply the above settings to the populated commodity code field in the shopping cart. Note –This option is only valid if Commodity Code mapping is being used.

While testing for 18.1 we compared the way UNSPSC values are exported in XML and in document search exports to the way it was done in 17.3. We found that the separator is completely ignored for exports in the 17.3 release. Therefore, we are not using these settings in 18.1 when we do an XML export of a document or when we perform a transaction or full export of a set of documents in document search. In the 17.3 release the field "Apply to UN/SPSC Integration Value" field is not being obeyed for XML exports. Therefore, we are not changing this behavior in 18.1. The setting indicates that both the masking format and separator formats should be used in integration points when this setting is equal to true. In 17.1 release we noted that the invoice transaction export does not have the UN/SPSC column or the commodity code column as part of this file structure. Therefore, we are leaving that alone and will not make changes to the invoice transaction export.
For more information about SCT Addresses:

- EP-1774 Add the GUI and Wiring for the SCT Addresses mapping on the new tab CLOSED Navigate to Setup > Hosted Catalog and Ordering Configuration > Category, Commodity and UOM Mapping Sets >Select the Default Mapping set, Select SCT Addresses. In order to manage this page, the user needs an administrative permission called Catalog Management. Generally this configuration is setup by an internal user or partner user, but it is accessible by regular users. Organizations with the Banner Finance ERP application are able to send a supplier synchronization message to the eProcurement application. This message keeps the eProcurement system synchronized with the Banner Finance system of record. Banner Finance allows the customer to define different types of supplier addresses. The eProcurement system needs a table that tells it how to interpret the different address types coming from Banner Finance. The eProcurement site administrator enters the values as they appear in Banner Finance and relates them to the type of address that should be created for the supplier profile in the eProcurement system. Some of our older Banner Finance customers like Virginia Tech = VATech (site name in switch org) use this table. Here is an example message for supplier synchronization. Notice the "type" attribute in the Address elements. <PurchasingAddress status="Active" type="Order Address" number="1"> = the primary fulfillment address <AccountsPayableAddress status="Active" type="Order Address" number="1"> = the primary remittance address <Address status="Active" type="Vendor Payment Address" number="1"> = a generic active remittance address

Question: Why does the SCT Address page show in organizations that do not use Banner Finance?

Answer: The SCT Addresses page appears in all orgs regardless of licenses because the eProcurement system does not currently have a reliable site profile setting to identify an org as having the Banner Finance integration features. If it becomes a problem for customers to see this page, please enter a feature request to add a site profile field that would allow an org to be flagged as a Banner Finance org. Then all customer orgs that have Banner Finance would need to be migrated to set this flag to true. This might involve an effort from account managers, customer support, implementation and customer success managers to go through and set the flag to true. This is just a suggestion on how we might solve this problem. Please enter a feature request and talk to Product Management about the issue.

In a future release, the ability to define multiple sets and pick one as your org default will be released. For now, everyone will see one set that has been migrated to the new tables in the CategoryUOMMappingSets schema.
